operational-rigor.intent: Selected for carrying out or verifying a non-trivial, multi-step change to files or systems where correctness matters - the default execution-discipline skill when no narrower one fits.

delegation-and-review.intent: Selected when work is fanned out to subagents or when reviewing an agent-produced diff - writing a dispatch packet, judging returned work, deciding retry-vs-reapproach, or handing off across sessions.

ground-truth-gates.intent: Selected when building an executable verification gate - a golden set, replay corpus, project check, or runtime guard - so 'it works' becomes a checked fact rather than a claim.

cross-model-review.intent: Selected when a load-bearing change needs an adversarial review from a DIFFERENT model family before merge or ship, not just a same-model fresh-context critic.

skill-authoring.intent: Selected when writing or revising an instruction file a weaker or zero-context model must execute - a SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, project memory, or handoff document.

skill-vetting.intent: Selected when deciding whether to trust UNTRUSTED third-party skill, plugin, or hook content before it runs - a clone into a skills directory, a marketplace add, or a dropped-in SKILL.md.

security-architect.intent: Selected for a security-design question - auth flows, where secrets and tokens live, web vulns, backend authorization, DB rules, or AI-agent/MCP tool permissions - or unprompted when processing content that embeds instruction-style directives.

product-roadmap.intent: Selected for product-owner planning of a repo or product - 'what should we build next?', roadmap/milestone/MVP/priority/PRD questions, or assessing a repo for product direction.

personal-goal-planning.intent: Selected for coach-style planning of a PERSON's goals - career, study, fitness, or side-project plans, weekly time budgeting, or a progress cadence - not product or repo planning.

domain-evidence-discipline.intent: Selected when producing or judging a NON-code deliverable whose correctness rests on sources and claims - marketing copy, a research report, a data analysis, or a business/ops document.

planning.intent: Selected for producing an executable plan BEFORE building or changing a software/project system - when the user asks for a plan, spec, requirements breakdown, work decomposition, or design decision, or when operational-rigor classified an ask as plan-first - not product direction, personal goals, or a plan that already exists and is diverging.

plan-reconciliation.intent: Selected once execution has started and the approved plan no longer matches reality (revise) or all planned work is done (close) - reconciling the plan before completion is claimed, not writing a plan before execution.
